newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil facilitates state bank privatizations.
newsitem.headline: Brazil facilitates state bank privatizations.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Saturday published a decree facilitating the sell-off of banks belonging to the states, officials said.

In a re-edited version of a previous decree on public sector banks, the government allowed federal Banco do Brasil, federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica and the National Development Bank (BNDES) to buy up credits from state banks have plans to restructure and be sold.
The purchase of the credits, seen as facilitating the transfer to the federal government of Sao Paulo state bank Banespa, will be financed by special credit lines.
If the returns on the assets acquired are lower than the interest charged on the Central Bank financing, the National Treasury could make up the difference, the decree said.

The measure is seen as helping Caixa Economica become Brazil's principal mortgage bank by financing the purchase of the mortgage portfolios of state banks, an aim Caixa president Sergio Cutulo has said is only possible with federal aid.
The decree on state banks was one of 23 re-edited decrees, five of which were altered, published in a special edition of the government's Official Journal Saturday.
